seo_meta_description: Master Sat Strategies on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Regression Formula for Coefficients
techniques.description: Use the tilde (~) operator to force Desmos to find the best-fit parameters for any function type. Perfect for finding constants in quadratic or exponential models.
techniques.when_to_use: When given a table of values and asked to find a specific constant or the value of a function at a point.
techniques.pro_tip: Always check the R^2 value; if it is 1, your model is a perfect fit.

techniques.title: Interactive Sliders for Unknowns
techniques.description: Type an equation with variables like 'a' or 'k' and click 'add slider'. Adjust the slider until the graph matches given constraints.
techniques.when_to_use: When solving for a constant that makes two lines intersect at a specific point or satisfy a condition.
techniques.pro_tip: Click the slider value to manually type in precise numbers.

techniques.title: Intersection Point Finder
techniques.description: Graph both sides of an equation as separate functions. Click the point where the lines cross to see the solution.
techniques.pro_tip: If the lines are parallel, the intersection is undefined; if they overlap, there are infinite solutions.

techniques.title: Evaluating Functions at Points
techniques.description: Define a function f(x) and then type f(number) in a new line to get the output instantly.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked to evaluate complex expressions or find the value of a function at a specific input.
techniques.pro_tip: Use this to check answer choices by plugging them into the function.

techniques.title: System of Inequalities Shading
techniques.description: Graph inequalities and look for the overlapping shaded region. Use curly brackets {} to restrict domains.
techniques.when_to_use: When asked which point (x, y) is a solution to a system of inequalities.
techniques.pro_tip: Type the point as (x, y) in a new line to see if it lands in the shaded region.

speed_walkthroughs.problem: If $3x + 7 = 22$, what is the value of $x$?

drills.question: Which of the following is a solution to $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$?
